chain_note: negative result, recorded at the same weight as a promotion
claim_tested: The near-extremal region can be reached by locating a Top-C tie point and perturbing it, so the m=6 structure transfers to other m as a seeding recipe.
consequence: The exact LP ascent is a LOCAL method. It climbs well when seeded inside the basin (1.000440 -> 1.0651 in 17 s, and -> 1.1999 as the StrictTopC margin is relaxed) but it does not find the basin. Testing the conjecture sup 2D/delta = m at m = 4 and m = 8 is therefore BLOCKED on seeding, not on compute.
diagnosis: The obstruction is not locating the tie point, it is the DIRECTION of departure from it. The extremal directions form a measure-zero set in the tangent directions at the tie point, so sampling them fails for the same reason isotropic sampling of worlds fails (addendum B Section 98.2).

status_of_the_conjecture: sup 2D/delta_square = m is supported at m=6 by a margin sweep converging to 1.2 = 6/5 with deficit linear in the margin (coefficient about 6.7). It is UNTESTED at every other m. Not promoted.

structure_measured_at_m6.extremal_matrix_note: F depends almost entirely on t = a cap complement(S); the multilinear form of that part is u + v - w + uv - uvw on Sc = {1,2,3}, plus a correction of [s nonempty] on three columns and [0 in a] on one. This is ONE vertex of the optimal face, not a canonical formula, which is why it was not generalized directly.

what_would_unblock: Solve for the direction instead of sampling it. At a tie point the limiting ratio along a direction d is a ratio of directional derivatives, and the Top-C selection is decided by the sign pattern of d on the tied scores. Maximizing the limit over d on the tangent cone at the tie point is again a linear-fractional problem, hence an LP over a finite set of sign patterns. That is a construction, not a search, and it would produce seeds at every m.
